comment: Triage ledger: every purl-level disagreement with a competitor tool is triaged as our-fn (we miss it), their-fp (they invent it), their-fn (they miss it), or intentional (design decision). A rationale is required, and a disagreement without an entry fails the differential job. Recorded against the syft version the scheduled job pins; `differential_harness.py --refresh` re-records competitor output, after which stale entries must be removed rather than left to rot.

entries.rationale: go.mod replaces acme/mux with gorilla/mux; sorb emits both sides joined by a RESOLVED_FROM edge so the SBOM shows what was asked for and what was built. syft emits only the replaced-to module under the original's name.
A go.sum entry with no go.mod requirement. Emitted with an explicit gosum-superset annotation rather than silently; syft skips sum-only modules. Revisit once full MVS resolution lands.
The package.json packageManager field is recorded as a build-tool component; syft ignores it.

A devDependency that is both locked and installed under node_modules. syft reports neither; sorb reports it at installed tier with scope=dev, so --scope runtime can drop it by choice instead of by omission.

Present in node_modules with no lockfile entry. syft does not catalog it; sorb reports it at installed tier with a drift:installed-not-declared annotation and reduced confidence — an unaccounted-for package on disk is exactly what an SBOM should surface.

syft does detect this package from the embedded rootfs dpkg status, but emits it with no purl because it finds no distro release file, so it is invisible to purl-level comparison. sorb assigns the deb/debian purl from the package DB itself.
Same as libc6: detected by both, but only sorb gives it a purl.
The scanned project itself. sorb models it as the document subject and a project node in the graph, not as one of its own dependencies.

poetry.lock is stale: it locks 2.31.0 while 2.32.0 is installed. syft emits both versions as separate components, implying both are present. sorb emits one component pinned to the installed 2.32.0 with a drift:locked-vs-installed annotation recording what the lock claimed.

Declared with an environment marker and never resolved to a version. sorb emits a versionless purl so downstream tooling still has an identity to match on, plus conditional=true; syft emits nothing for unresolved declarations.
A build-system requirement with no resolved version. Emitted with a versionless purl and scope=build so it can be filtered by choice; syft does not report build-system requires.
